title: Defixionum Tabellae Atticae (Wünsch 1897) with Audollent, Defixionum Tabellae (1904); RU «Аттические таблички с проклятиями»
author: Anonymous (curse-tablet writers)
size: DTA c. 220 tablets; DT c. 305; mostly short
edition: Wünsch, IG III.3 appendix (1897) and Audollent (1904), both public domain on archive.org; later finds in Jordan's SGD
ru_evidence: Russian articles with excerpts: «Судебная магия в классической Греции» (2010), «Связывающие проклятия… классических Афин» (2023), Philologia Classica (2019) on similia formulae. No corpus translation.
en_evidence: Gager, Curse Tablets and Binding Spells (1992), a selection (BMCR 1993.02.03); Eidinow 2007 catalogue of binding curses
other_translations: German for the Latin curses (Kropp 2008, from memory); no full Greek corpus translation found
value: Direct evidence for magic, law-court and commercial rivalries, theatre and love; names of real Athenians; non-elite language. Much used in religion, law and sociolinguistics.
ai_feasibility: medium: formulaic, but misspellings, voces magicae and fragments. A good showcase for visible critical apparatus and model disagreement.
pilot_unit: DTA judicial and commercial curses, c. 100 tablets, c. 3–4k words
